summary: The pattern becomes more useful when memory maintenance is treated as ordinary repository maintenance rather than a separate knowledge-management programme, and when the rest of the operating model is read through it.

items.text: Validate index targets, duplicate identifiers, broken links, descriptor enums and supersession cycles in continuous integration; a descriptor outside its enum should render as invalid, not disappear.
Display recalled file paths, revisions and per-page agent read counts alongside agent output so an operator can inspect the effective context.
Assign review intervals by consequence: command syntax and operational policy expire faster than historical rationale.
Connect durable memory to the existing pattern for searchable decisions rather than creating a parallel decision archive.
Classify an assertion as working, episodic, semantic or procedural memory before applying durable-memory maintenance rules.
Load memory through small, explicit context entry points instead of injecting the whole folder into every run.
Give the memory a navigable, bidirectional surface: graphical overview pages, decision history, meta companions and read counters make the folder a cognitive interface rather than an archive.
Keep page-level metadata — related tasks, grades, classification — in predictably named companion files beside the page so the memory can be surveyed without opening every document.
Read pull-request-free delivery through this layer: gate standards, override rules and requeue reasons are memory, and the verdict stream is only legible while they are kept current.
